title: ZuriQ Secures $25.5M Seed Round and Advances 2D Trapped-Ion Fabrication with Infineon - Quantum Computing Report
gist: ETH Zurich spinout ZuriQ raised a $25.5M seed led by Quantonation to scale micro-Penning trap quantum computing, replacing RF Paul traps with static fields so qubit density scales quadratically with chip area instead of linearly with ion-chain length. Removing RF also removes substrate heating, which is what makes the design manufacturable on Infineon's standard silicon CMOS production lines — the company has already run a nine-ion 3x3 array and is building a 40-ion processor.

insights.claim: Swiss quantum hardware startup ZuriQ raised $25.5 million (EUR 22.4M) in seed funding led by Quantonation, with participation from Forward.one, Extantia, Firgun Ventures, and existing early-stage investors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A $25.5M seed is large for European deep tech and signals specialist quantum funds still underwrite architecture risk at pre-revenue stage.
insights.locator: Swiss quantum hardware startup ZuriQ has raised

insights.claim: The company was spun out of ETH Zurich in 2024 by Dr. Pavel Hrmo, Dr. Tobias Sagesser, and Dr. Shreyans Jain, and the seed builds on a $4.2 million pre-seed round raised in 2025.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A roughly 6x step-up in round size within about a year implies investors validated the 3x3 demonstrator milestone — a fast graduation cadence worth tracking for the Series A.
insights.locator: Spun out of ETH Zürich in 2024

insights.claim: The funding will expand an 18-person technical team that has already recruited talent from IonQ, Xanadu, and Hamamatsu, and will scale chip fabrication throughput with Infineon.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Talent flowing out of listed quantum incumbents toward a seed-stage European startup is a soft signal about relative conviction in competing architectures.
insights.locator: With its seed capital in place

themes.theme: Micro-Penning traps versus the RF Paul trap scaling ceiling

insights.claim: Legacy trapped-ion architectures rely on radio-frequency Paul traps that constrain ions into single-file 1D chains stitched together via complex physical grid junctions, which is the fundamental scaling limit ZuriQ targets.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Junction-based shuttling is the known cost driver in incumbent trapped-ion roadmaps; any architecture that removes junctions attacks the incumbents' hardest engineering problem.
insights.locator: ZuriQ’s hardware platform addresses a fundamental scaling limit

insights.claim: By replacing rapidly oscillating RF electric fields with static magnetic and electric fields in micro-Penning traps, ZuriQ's architecture allows ions to move freely in two and three dimensions without physical junction bottlenecks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is the core technical bet — if static-field trapping holds fidelity at scale, it changes the cost curve for the entire trapped-ion category.

insights.claim: Under the micro-Penning design, qubit density scales quadratically with the surface area of the chip rather than linearly with chain length, laying an architectural foundation for multi-thousand-qubit systems.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quadratic-versus-linear scaling is the crispest quantitative argument in the pitch; it implies the qubit-count gap with 1D trapped-ion incumbents could close abruptly rather than gradually.
insights.quote: qubit density scales quadratically with the surface area of the chip rather than linearly with chain length

insights.claim: ZuriQ established a strategic foundry partnership with Infineon Technologies AG to co-develop advanced ion-trap chips using industrial semiconductor fabrication lines, with Infineon bringing over half a decade of specialized trapped-ion chip manufacturing experience.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Infineon is quietly accumulating a position as Europe's trapped-ion foundry of record — a picks-and-shovels exposure to the category that trades on automotive semiconductor multiples.
insights.locator: A key pillar of ZuriQ’s commercial roadmap

insights.claim: Because the static-field Penning design eliminates high-voltage, high-frequency RF signals that typically dissipate heat into the chip substrate, it allows straightforward integration into standard silicon CMOS processes.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: CMOS compatibility is the difference between artisanal lab devices and volume manufacturing — it is the argument that this architecture can ride semiconductor cost curves.
insights.quote: bridging the gap between academic physics experiments and mass-producible quantum chips
insights.locator: Because ZuriQ’s static-field Penning technology eliminates

insights.claim: The design goal is explicitly framed as bridging the gap between academic physics experiments and mass-producible quantum chips, positioning manufacturability rather than raw qubit performance as the differentiator.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Diligence should focus on yield and process maturity data from Infineon's lines rather than on headline fidelity numbers.
insights.locator: bridging the gap between academic physics experiments

insights.claim: ZuriQ validated its design with a working nine-ion 3x3 demonstrator array described as the largest two-dimensional array of its kind to date, built within 18 months with ETH Zurich and fabricated on Infineon's production lines.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Nine ions is tiny in absolute terms — the investment case rests on the scaling slope, not the current device, so the 40-ion step is the milestone that matters.
insights.locator: The company has validated its design through a working nine-ion

insights.claim: Foundational results published in Nature and Science Advances demonstrated arbitrary 2D and 3D ion shuttling and two-qubit gate operations in micro-Penning traps.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Peer-reviewed two-qubit gates in Penning traps de-risk the physics; remaining risk is engineering and yield, which is a different and more fundable risk profile.
insights.locator: This milestone follows foundational experimental achievements

insights.claim: ZuriQ is developing a next-generation 40-ion processor as a stepping stone toward full chip-scale scaling, with the stated end goal of trapped-ion processors capable of supporting industrially relevant fault-tolerant workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The 40-ion device is the next binary checkpoint — delivery on schedule would justify a Series A markup, slippage would reset the quadratic-scaling narrative.
insights.locator: ZuriQ is currently leveraging this industrial process
